Once you have assembled your analysis dataset ([Phase
12](data-manipulation.qmd)), you are ready to analyse. This section stays
**register-specific and practical**: when to use what, which packages, and a
minimal example - it does not teach statistical theory. For depth, see the
[Epidemiologist R Handbook](https://www.epirhandbook.com/en/), [R for Data
Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) and DDEA's R course (see [Learning
resources](learning-resources.qmd)).

## Pages in this section

Pick the pages that fit your study - not every study uses all of them.

  | Page                                                         | Packages                                                                            |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | [Choosing a statistical analysis](choosing-analysis.qmd) | `stats` (base R; choose test and model)                                             |
  | [Descriptive tables (Table 1)](descriptive-tables.qmd)   | `gtsummary`, `finalfit`                                                             |
  | [Figures for publication](figures.qmd)                   | `ggplot2`                                                                           |
  | [Regression](regression.qmd)                             | `glm`/`lm`, `survival::clogit` (matched case-control)                               |
  | [Time-to-event](time-to-event.qmd)                       | `survival`, `survminer`, `tidycmprsk` (Cox, competing risks)                        |
  | [Rates and rate ratios (Poisson)](rates-poisson.qmd)     | `glm` (Poisson), `MASS::glm.nb`, `Epi`/`popEpi` (incidence rate ratio, person-time) |
  | [IP weighting (IPTW and IPCW)](weighting-iptw.qmd)       | `WeightIt`, `cobalt` (confounding + censoring/missing outcomes)                     |
  | [Sensitivity analyses](sensitivity-analyses.qmd)         | `survival` (robustness checks, negative control outcome, active comparator)         |

::: {.callout-important}
**Output control decides what you can compute, not just what you can send.**
Only aggregated results leave DST, and cells below the threshold (3 or 5
observations, depending on your project) may not be repatriated at all. That
shapes the analysis itself: how finely you may stratify a table, whether a
subgroup is worth running, whether a figure can show what you want. Plan for it
here rather than discovering it at the end. The rules and the threshold are on
[Phase 14 - Export and repatriation](export.qmd).
:::
